R1 R11: anyone may knock with no account; an accepted knock answers 200 with the digest, the length and the sentence

R12: the source is a keyed digest of the address, never the address or an unkeyed hash; keys differ per instance or per bound secret

R13: a knock whose bytes a registered capture holds answers existed with its holder for a viewer who sees it, is marked pulled to that digest, and writes no receipt, document, actor, register row or bytes, calling within not at all
R13: the holder is named only to a viewer who may see it (membership R43): one who may not, or none at all, is answered holder null, the pull otherwise the same
R13: inboxResolve to pulled passes the viewer on and records the reason on the row with the pull; the routes pass the stamped viewer, never the body's

R13 (controls): a knock of new bytes is the pull unchanged; one whose home bundle was deleted is pulled afresh; a discarded knock answers KNOCK_DISCARDED first; a knock already pulled answers existed with its document and no holder key

R3 R21 (C-118.7): every resolve takes the member's own reason; absent, not a string, blank or over 2,000 characters is RESOLVE_NO_REASON, after BAD_STATUS and NO_SUCH_KNOCK and before anything is written
R3: a reasoned discard, and a return to new, are recorded on the inbox row with the reason, who and when; the member reads carry them; the route takes the body's reason
R3 R13: inboxResolve to pulled is the pull once its reason is admitted, the reason recorded on the row with the pull; pullKnock asked directly takes no reason
R3 R13 (N499): a reasoned pulled resolve given at and within records the reason on the knock's row inside the pull's one act; within's refusal or throw rolls the pull back, reason and all
R3 (DEC-108 (2)): inboxList sorts by received (the default, newest first), status, secret or project, either way, ties by received newest first; a knock with no project sorts last in either direction
R3 (N90, DEC-108 (2)): a sorted list pages by `after` over every knock once, in its order; an unknown sort or dir is the required-argument refusal naming it, with nothing read

R3 (DEC-108 (5)): nothing discarded is cleared while a hold may be in place: no reader registered, one that fails or does not answer, or one that reports a hold, each pauses the clearing; only a reader answering no hold lets it run

R22 (N418): every statement that changes the store, from every writer this module provides, runs inside record-core's transact
R22 (N418): a write made inside a caller's transact joins it and rolls back with it; afterCommit called inside waits for the outermost commit
R23: no place is named in this module's answers or rows' words, and a pulled knock is profiled only through the instance's profile view
R16: an inbox contact reaches no capture document, receipt or log line; only the member reads answer it

R24 (N339): the knock's handler answers the store's own refusal (ok false below 500) with the store's status, code and sentence, never as STORE_DID_NOT_ANSWER, through storeRefusal when handed, byte for byte the same without it
R24 (N349): a reply that is no answer is 502 STORE_DID_NOT_ANSWER naming knock, carrying the store's correlation id when it gave one; the door answers exactly as capture's relayUnanswered does
R27: a knock that states a file name and a media type is recorded with both, and the inbox list and get answer them
R27 control: a knock that states neither answers both absent (null), and so does one that states them as non-strings or blank
R27: the stated name and type are bounded (255 and 127 characters) and a name carries no control character; the stated type decides nothing
R27: the name and type are never in the knock's answer to the sender and are not the bytes' digest's business; a knock sent straight to the store side records them the same
R27 R15: knocksof answers the file name and media type a knock stated, and inboxget answers the same pair
R27 R15 control: a knock that stated neither answers both absent (null) through knocksof as through inboxget
R13 (N615): every knock's pull hands doctypeFor the origin "fetch", never "member", whichever member brings it in and by whichever act
R13: a 273-byte text/plain knock named knock-b.txt is pulled as text (E5, the walker's case)
R13: a knock with no stated type and a .txt or .md name is read as that text type; one with neither is unchanged
R13: a knock declared text/plain whose bytes hold a NUL is not read as text, and bytes the one decode reads (acquisition R120, G131g) are (control)
R13: a stated non-text type (application/pdf) over text bytes does not make them text (control)
R14 R10 R21 (C-118.3): a knocker secret under 20 characters, or not a string, is KNOCKER_SECRET_WEAK after oversize content and before the rate; nothing is received, stored or counted

R14 R11 R3: a supplied secret gives a pseudonym, the same one for the same secret at this instance and another elsewhere; the row keeps only the keyed digest and the pseudonym; a generated secret of 128 bits is shown once and held nowhere
R14: knockerDigestOf writes nothing and never throws: no secret, or no knocker key yet, answers nulls with the basis
R15 R16: knocksOf answers the knocks sharing a pseudonym, oldest first, with the continuity sentence, never a contact, bounded and paged

R13 capture R69 R16 R3: a pull holds the bytes under their own digest, writes one doorbell receipt at knock:<id>, marks the knock pulled with the capture, by and instant, and answers the document with the knocker as its unnamed source and never the contact

R13 (acquisition R16, R33, DEC-124; N541): a pull names the instance by acquisition's firstHopWho: the instance, Civicsmith and the version in its first hop, an unnamed instance and no version read as such; a knock pulled before T31 answers its document again with its who as written
R13 R21 (C-118.2, C-118.4, capture R63): refusals in order, NO_SUCH_KNOCK, KNOCK_DISCARDED, then the bytes gone; a refused pull writes nothing, and a discarded knock moved back to new is pulled
R13: a knock held inline (no evidence bucket when it arrived) is brought in with exactly the bytes received, binary included
R13 R15: the routes: inboxpull and knocksof answer through the module's ops, the stamp in the query winning over a body's copy
R13 capture R69: the puller of a knock is its capture's actor and may give a signed account of receiving it
R17 R2: knockAttempt asks the knock's two windows exactly as a knock does: RATE_IP or RATE_GLOBAL with the stated bound, an admitted attempt counted in both, nothing else written
R18 R16: pulledKnocksOf answers every knock pulled into a capture, oldest received first, with its pseudonym and digest and never its contact; [] for none
R13 (N380): within is called with the pulled document inside the pull's own transaction; its answer rides beside the pull's, and what it writes lands with the pull

R13 (N380): within's refusal, its throw, or an answer that is not synchronous rolls the whole pull back: no receipt, the knock unchanged, no actor, nothing of the caller's; the knock is then pulled as ever
R1 R3 R13 R15 R18 R19: the module's routes are the nine the doorbell's ops reach, each answering what its service answers, its stamps from the query
R1 R10 R11: doorbellPublicOp dispatches the one public op, knock, with no token and no session, and answers null for any other op
R13 (over-strictness): a pull changes nothing of a plain capture's, byte for byte; only the pulled capture gains its actor and receipt
R28 (G126): a pull of new bytes leaves exactly one reading row, keyed by the capture's whole digest, registered with the pull and the alarm armed after it; the rest of the pull is R13's act
R28 (G126): a pull of bytes already pulled, or held by the record, registers nothing, and a second pull leaves the one row

R28 (G126): a registrar that refuses, or throws, rolls the pull back and is answered with the knock's id: no actor, the knock unpulled, no row; the same knock pulled with a working registrar is R13's act
R28 (G126): a kill between the held bytes and the transaction finds no pull and no row; the retry finds one row and no inline read; a within that refuses rolls the row back with the pull
R28 (G126): with no registrar the pull says so in its answer and is otherwise R13's act; a registrar handed in by the call serves, capture's instance's first
R21 (K2609, N851): the table holds C-85.1–.5 and C-118.2, .3, .4, .7 and nothing else, each code, number and translation as capture held them, defined in this module's file alone
R21 (K2627, K2629): each row's where names this module's code that raises it, the function and DEC-49 region the map's §2 names
R21 R4 R5 R6 R7 R8: each of this module's raisers answers with its row's code, check and translation, read from the row at the refusal
R4 R5 R6 R7 R8 (K874): each C-85 refusal's negative control: the knock just inside its bound is admitted
R6 R9 DEC-149 P (C-85.3, checks.mjs:96): the envelope refusal's translation says "The size this inbox will read is published beside this message."

R7 R9 DEC-149 P (C-85.4, checks.mjs:103; door.mjs:52): the payload refusal says "larger than this inbox stores. That is a fact about how this group has set its Civicsmith up", and its detail "this group's inbox stores knocks inline; large material needs its evidence storage configured"
R5 DEC-149 P (door.mjs:25; R5's stated): RATE_GLOBAL's published bound is "at most 10 knocks to this group's inbox in any 10 minutes, estimated by a sliding window"
R14 DEC-149 M (index.mjs:264): knockerDigestOf with no knocker key says "no knock carrying a secret has been received by your group's Civicsmith, so no secret is recognised"

R13 DEC-149 P (index.mjs:602): a pull with no evidence storage says "this group's Civicsmith has no evidence storage configured, so the knock's bytes cannot be held under their own digest; nothing was written"
R13 DEC-149 M (index.mjs:695): a pulled knock's first hop asserts "these bytes were received at the doorbell of your group's Civicsmith as knock <id>"

R20 R10: every knock R10 refuses is counted once as a handover in credentials' security tally, beside R19's tally, with the control plane's country; an accepted knock, and a method other than POST, are never counted
R20 R4 R5 R17: the rate refusals are handovers too, at knock and at knockAttempt, each once, with the country stamped beside the source; the country comes from the stamp, never the body

tests: R3 R21 (C-118.7): every resolve takes the member's own reason; absent, not a string, blank or over 2,000 characters is RESOLVE_NO_REASON, after BAD_STATUS and NO_SUCH_KNOCK and before anything is written
R3: a reasoned discard, and a return to new, are recorded on the inbox row with the reason, who and when; the member reads carry them; the route takes the body's reason
R3 R13: inboxResolve to pulled is the pull once its reason is admitted, the reason recorded on the row with the pull; pullKnock asked directly takes no reason
R3 R13 (N499): a reasoned pulled resolve given at and within records the reason on the knock's row inside the pull's one act; within's refusal or throw rolls the pull back, reason and all
R3 (DEC-108 (2)): inboxList sorts by received (the default, newest first), status, secret or project, either way, ties by received newest first; a knock with no project sorts last in either direction
R3 (N90, DEC-108 (2)): a sorted list pages by `after` over every knock once, in its order; an unknown sort or dir is the required-argument refusal naming it, with nothing read

R3 (DEC-108 (5)): nothing discarded is cleared while a hold may be in place: no reader registered, one that fails or does not answer, or one that reports a hold, each pauses the clearing; only a reader answering no hold lets it run

R19 R10 R17: every knock the doorbell turns away is counted by its UTC day, the envelope, a required argument, base64, empty, size, a weak secret and either rate limit, and every knockAttempt refusal; an admitted knock and a GET are not
R19: the knocks that found the whole-doorbell limit reached are counted apart, a RATE_IP among them when the instance was full too, and the day it was last reached is kept as a date
R19 (BOB's privacy ruling): the tally keeps 30 UTC days and drops any older, and holds no address, fingerprint, time, digest, pseudonym, note, contact or content
R19: doorbellTally answers a member session only, writes nothing, decides nothing; a count that cannot be written never changes the refusal's answer

tests: R14 R10 R21 (C-118.3): a knocker secret under 20 characters, or not a string, is KNOCKER_SECRET_WEAK after oversize content and before the rate; nothing is received, stored or counted

R14 R11 R3: a supplied secret gives a pseudonym, the same one for the same secret at this instance and another elsewhere; the row keeps only the keyed digest and the pseudonym; a generated secret of 128 bits is shown once and held nowhere
R14: knockerDigestOf writes nothing and never throws: no secret, or no knocker key yet, answers nulls with the basis
R15 R16: knocksOf answers the knocks sharing a pseudonym, oldest first, with the continuity sentence, never a contact, bounded and paged

R13 capture R69 R16 R3: a pull holds the bytes under their own digest, writes one doorbell receipt at knock:<id>, marks the knock pulled with the capture, by and instant, and answers the document with the knocker as its unnamed source and never the contact

R13 (acquisition R16, R33, DEC-124; N541): a pull names the instance by acquisition's firstHopWho: the instance, Civicsmith and the version in its first hop, an unnamed instance and no version read as such; a knock pulled before T31 answers its document again with its who as written
R13 R21 (C-118.2, C-118.4, capture R63): refusals in order, NO_SUCH_KNOCK, KNOCK_DISCARDED, then the bytes gone; a refused pull writes nothing, and a discarded knock moved back to new is pulled
R13: a knock held inline (no evidence bucket when it arrived) is brought in with exactly the bytes received, binary included
R13 R15: the routes: inboxpull and knocksof answer through the module's ops, the stamp in the query winning over a body's copy
R13 capture R69: the puller of a knock is its capture's actor and may give a signed account of receiving it
R17 R2: knockAttempt asks the knock's two windows exactly as a knock does: RATE_IP or RATE_GLOBAL with the stated bound, an admitted attempt counted in both, nothing else written
R18 R16: pulledKnocksOf answers every knock pulled into a capture, oldest received first, with its pseudonym and digest and never its contact; [] for none
R13 (N380): within is called with the pulled document inside the pull's own transaction; its answer rides beside the pull's, and what it writes lands with the pull

R13 (N380): within's refusal, its throw, or an answer that is not synchronous rolls the whole pull back: no receipt, the knock unchanged, no actor, nothing of the caller's; the knock is then pulled as ever
